steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Hey, wing-man.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I'm talking to you! Hey, come back!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Assuming that 'wing-man' is an epithet for Sankta, there are multiple individuals who fit the name.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I'm talking to you. I know your name is Federico.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: You really know how to piss people off, don't you?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I don't have time for your crap.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: That guy, Oren...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: He said that Gerald, he... for us, for me and Fortuna...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Is it true? Is Gerald really—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes, Gerald is dead.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Now that you answered, I'm starting to wish you didn't.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I don't get it... how could it be...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, but this is a fact.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Ha... what are you sorry about?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Bah...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Keep your distance, wing-man. Close your eyes. Don't look at me.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: That thing on your head is way too bright. It hurts my eyes. I just need a second to adjust.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Gerald gave you his knife. The choice was his. It's not my place to argue.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: But I can't let you take it away.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: You have to know what it means to take the weapon of a Sarkaz mercenary.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It means carrying on the legacy of his name.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Yes. That's why I'm going to take it back from you, along with Gerald's name, and his honor.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I challenge you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You won't win.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I have to.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: As long as I draw breath, I'll find you, and challenge you.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Don't you dare underestimate me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I refuse your challenge.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: H-How dare you?!

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I'm challenging you to an honorable—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Gerald was a mere hunter. There is no legacy to inherit in this knife.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Exactly what I said.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you want a knife that inherited the name of a Sarkaz mercenary, I have never been in possession of one. You're wasting your time challenging me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you want the knife of Gerald the Hunter, then yes, I am currently in possession of it.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Why you...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do you want it?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: ...Burdenbeast dung.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: This was Gerald's treasure. He wouldn't never let me take it just like that.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: You keep it safe.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: You just wait... I'll lead my people to find a new path, just like Gerald did.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I'll come back for it when I've earned it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will keep it safe, until then.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Raimund...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Stop gawking. I think he can take it.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: What about you? You said you couldn't hold a gun anymore. Are you... praying with it?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I have a feeling it will answer me again.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Can I still use it, Serpilia?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Why not? It may be a little old, but you can trust my handiwork.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I used to study antique guns, you know.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Lately, though, I'm finding new things a little more interesting.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Do new things scare you at all?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: There's no point being scared. One wants to learn more, in spite of the fear.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Besides...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Somebody once told me that techniques exist to be used.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I didn't understand at the time. But now...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Now?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I understand a little. I'm a craftsman, and I'm responsible for the weapons I craft.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Well, set that aside for a bit. What about you?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Are you ready to leave with the Sarkaz?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: H-How did you know what I was going to say?!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: No empathy needed to guess your thoughts.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: It's not such a big deal when you put it that way, is it?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You wouldn't come looking for me at this hour with that solemn look on your face, if you were planning to come back to Laterano.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: ...Sorry.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I promised to come quietly and accept the punishment I deserved... but now I'm trying to run away.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: S-So...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: So, will I let you go?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Take a guess.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Your whole deal here is kind of a headache. You'll have to wear a hood all the time, if you live in Laterano.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I-I see, I guess that won't work...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Not that it'll be much better anywhere else.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You'll need to hide your horns, your appearance, and your gun.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: And I'll still be your warden. You'll have to keep in touch with me, no matter where you go, as long as you live.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: You won't cause me any trouble, will you?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: —Er, um.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Wait, you're letting me go? W-Won't you get into trouble for that?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Worst case scenario, I quit my job at the Curia.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: That was a joke.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: It's true that I'll have some reports to write when I get back. I'll think about whether to get started on a resignation letter after that.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Anyway, you owe me more than a pizzelle now.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Th-Thank you... thank you so much.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Are we... still kin?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Does it matter? You're not getting off the hook, kin or not.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I want those pizzella next time I see you.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: The convoy is almost here. The abbey can start moving once it's refueled.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Well, this was a tricky case, even though the location wasn't that far from Laterano. I think I should borrow a bed at the abbey, get some rest.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: I didn't see you do anything particularly tiring, Richele.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Weren't you pretending that you didn't know anything?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Or should I thank you for not being lazy enough to dump all the evidence linked to the Church of the Deep into the sewers?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Don't be so uptight, Oren.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'm sure Federico remembers the Sarkaz mercenary's dossier better than I do. And you and Lemuen are definitely more familiar with Church of the Deep cases than I am.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Plus, don't you think we're starting to get along a little bit, after you gave up empathy?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Why are you bringing that up?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: No reason. Just, sometimes it's better to know less about a guy, like how you have to close one eye when you shoot.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Just to make it clear, though, I took Lemuen's instructions about confirming whether the abbey had anything to do with the Church of the Deep seriously.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: At the end of the day, I suppose we can all sleep better at night.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You're lucky... or should I say, we're lucky.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The monastery gets the supplies it needs to return to Laterano. The disruption to the inhabitants was minimal.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: The fallen girl has gone with the Sarkaz. Laterano will be able to find her, and the Sarkaz, if need be.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Laterano's image has not been materially affected.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Things don't turn out so well every day.

steps.name: Male Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: I prayed for a smooth trip to Laterano, safe from bandit attacks.

steps.name: Male Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: We should be fine once we get to Laterano.

steps.name: Female Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: I hope so! The emissaries from Laterano don't look like they've ever been hungry, and their clothes are brand new. I envy them.

steps.name: Female Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: How do they plant their crops? Or do they give everyone a gun to hunt with?

steps.name: Male Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Who knows? I can't imagine. I can't imagine what I would do with my time, if I didn't have to spend all my time fixing houses and making tools.

steps.name: Female Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: I'm trembling, and I can't tell whether it's from excitement or fear.

steps.name: Male Monastery Inhabitant
steps.text: Let's pray. Our faith will protect us.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Well, we did our best, didn't we?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: As for whether things will turn out well in the end...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Do you know where Mamma went?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: A child? I thought everyone was gathered up here.

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Mamma's not here... but she came back last night!

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Yeah, Mamma brought us a gift last night. We lent it to a sleeping man...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Sleeping?

steps.name: Estara & Erendel
steps.text: He was sleeping really deep! He must have been having a nice dream.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: An abbey built upon a mobile plate, moving again after being stranded for a decade, almost becoming one with the land...

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: An impressive sight, the convergence of destruction and rebirth.

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: You seem troubled. Do tell, if you feel unwell.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: Your transformation is yet incomplete. The path ahead will be laborious.

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: I'm fine.

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: They...

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: Will the Laterans treat those children well?

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: I believe so. The sitting pope is known for moderation and benevolence. They will likely be taken in by foster parents and grow up in Laterano.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: Traveling with the fallen angel, and with the eyes of Sankta from the Curia on them, it is unlikely that your kin will face any retribution.

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: I'm glad to hear that...

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: Only one thing, Bishop Aulus.

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: They're not my kin anymore.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: If that is what you think, then that is what it will be.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: The stranded Paradise is no more. It is time for us to set out.

steps.name: Aulus
steps.text: Once again, we welcome you, Hyman.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What are your plans?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Sinners cannot be choosers.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You may have had the intention to cause harm, but at the end of the day, you didn't do any real damage.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Personally, I see no problem, but Velliv might be a little stricter where Iberia is concerned...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Ah, it doesn't seem like you're very happy with that answer.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I apologize for the discourtesy I showed, Reverend Nuncio.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I sense your sincerity. I accept your apology.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But I also sense that it's not what you really want to say.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: It's not an easy thing, judging oneself...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: It is the truth that I fell to despair, and knelt before the malice in my heart.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What is more deserving of punishment: Harm caused out of benevolence, or malice not put into action?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: To me, it's the former.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: An idea could be fleeting, or it could take root silently, biding its time.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: How could you know that this is simply the result of a single moment of weakness?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: What would this place be like, if I chose another path?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I can't say that I've purged the caprices from my mind... I can't even say that I still believe in our laws...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But you still feel it, don't you?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Yes, I do...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Every waking moment, I prayed that the people would be given their due, prayed that this little corner of Paradise would not slip through my fingers.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: But I've waited for so long...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Too long. So long that I began to doubt that the very existence of faith was simply a self-imposed conceit.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: How does it feel?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Despair, fear, sorrow... what else? The feeling of...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Incredulity.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: How do we doubt something that exists in one's own mind?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: It means you've begun to doubt yourself... with terrible consequences, if one is unable to dispel the doubt.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: If even faith could be false, then how much of Stefano is real?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I wanted to understand. I tried to understand. But I overestimated myself.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We could never truly understand another. 'Understanding' remains precious, fleeting, even with the incredible power of empathy.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: But having experienced so much, I have began to think that there are many emotions that can be communicated from one to another, and understood by most, even without the empathy.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: At least, I can say that I have began to understand the thoughts of a certain individual, not because I sensed something, but because I have experienced it myself...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I offer this to you, Bishop Stefano.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: It's...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The notebook of a cleric who spent some time here. I thought you might find it... interesting.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Perhaps, just like you, he had many questions, and many troubles.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: You asked me about my plans.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I plan to return to Laterano. But not with the others.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You mean you want to travel from here to Laterano by yourself?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: At your age...?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Please don't stop me. I must know. I must... rediscover my faith.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: If there comes a day when I atone for my sins, if there is truly such a thing as miracles, perhaps I will find my Laterano then.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: In that case...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I wish you the best of luck.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I hope you find your answer, Father Stefano.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We will meet again in Paradise.
The old man says no more.
Age has taken its toll on him, as have the ordeals of last night. The lines of age fill every gap on his face.
Before Lemuen's eyes, Stefano Torregrossa walks out the door, his back slightly hunched.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Executor Federico, reporting in.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As previously reported, the two nuncios are confirmed alive and well. They are expected to return to their posts in Laterano soon.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Plans are in place for Sanctilaminium Ambrosii to resume movement, setting a course for Laterano's outskirts. It is expected to arrive at its destination before Spring next year.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: A request for supplies has been made to the Curia to ensure reliable mobility, and to meet the everyday needs of the inhabitants.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Forty-one of the one hundred fifty-three inhabitants of the monastery will depart the abbey. Serpilia will track and report on their subsequent movements.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The Sarkaz you mentioned?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I must admit my surprise, even though I had a hunch...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Whether it was the state of the abbey, the movements of the Church of the Deep, or Arturia...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You've done well, Federico.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I failed to meet your expectations.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Our intervention destabilized the situation at the abbey.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There were... three casualties.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You have doubts, my child.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I can rectify a wrong if I see it. I know many ways of stopping a sinner.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But at no point during this mission was there a clear course of action.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why was the result suboptimal, if no error was committed?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Are our laws suitable for all circumstances? If not, on what do I base my actions?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That is where my doubts lie.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I don't have an answer for you, Federico, because this is a question that troubles me as well.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But I'm happy that you're beginning to ask these questions.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I don't understand.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: There is no need to be anxious. You're beginning to ask questions that you've never considered before. Is that not a big step forward?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It's like pulling the cork from a bottle of fine wine. The hardest part is over. All that is left is to pour out what you want.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I'm going out to visit a friend, one that you're not unfamiliar with. I'll take your question to him.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: And share with you the answer he offers.
The towering statue is silent. The rays of the morning sun pour in. The executor ends the call and looks up.
The aging Sankta's silhouette begins to fade into the morning sun as he slowly walks away.
As she sees him off, Lemuen gets a feeling.
The feeling that she has not seen the last of the old man.
As he said himself—
Perhaps he will find the Laterano that he is looking for.
